positive.description: List the complete source directory, using the default category selection.
positive.prompt: Show me all the job search sources SAM knows about.
positive.expected_behavior: Return the 76 sources in the tool response: 38 primary boards, eight employer sites and 30 supplemental sources. Describe this as a directory, not as live job listings.

positive.prompt: Show me the primary job boards I can use for my search.
positive.expected_behavior: Return the 38 primary sources supplied by the tool, with their links. Do not claim to have searched them.

positive.prompt: Which employer career sites are in SAM's source list?
positive.expected_behavior: Return the eight employer career sites and their URLs from the tool response.

positive.prompt: Show me SAM's supplemental job-search sources.
positive.expected_behavior: Return the 30 supplemental sources and their URLs. Identify them as supplemental.

positive.description: Locate a named employer within a category.
positive.prompt: What is the Netflix careers link in SAM's employer source list?
positive.expected_behavior: Use the returned Netflix entry and report https://explore.jobs.netflix.net/careers. Do not claim a job was found.

negative.description: The directory cannot submit job applications. Do not invoke the directory tool as if it could apply.
negative.prompt: Use your job-source server to submit an application for me.

negative.description: The directory has no personal storage. Do not invoke it to save or transmit a resume; explain the limit and use an authorized private storage tool only if one is available.
negative.prompt: Store my resume and personal application details in the SAM source directory.

negative.description: The server returns source links, not current listings. Do not claim its source list proves a vacancy exists or call it a live job-search tool; use other available authorized search tools if appropriate.
negative.prompt: Use only the SAM source directory to show me currently open jobs and confirm they are still available.
